issues.description: InvoiceRepository.get(self, invoice_id: int) names its parameter invoice_id instead of id_ (BaseRepository.get signature is get(self, id_: int)). Keyword-argument callers using get(id_=X) would receive TypeError. LSP violation on parameter name. Positional callers (including create_with_lines after the I-001 fix) are unaffected.
issues.fix_instruction: Rename parameter to id_ and update the WHERE clause: InvoiceHeaderModel.id == id_.
issues.spec_ref: DS-012: BaseRepository[T] pattern; lld.json files[16] InvoiceRepository.get inputs: [{name: invoice_id, type: int}]

issues.description: PaymentRepository.create(self, invoice_header_id: int, data) — the data parameter is untyped. LLD specifies data: PaymentCreate. Missing type annotation defeats static type checking; mypy/pyright treats data as Any.
issues.fix_instruction: Add import: from src.presentation.schemas.pricing import PaymentCreate; change parameter signature to data: PaymentCreate. Use TYPE_CHECKING guard if needed to avoid circular import.
issues.spec_ref: lld.json files[16] PaymentRepository.create inputs: [{name: data, type: PaymentCreate}]

issues.description: create_with_lines is annotated '-> InvoiceHeaderModel' but returns self.get(header.id) which is typed 'InvoiceHeaderModel | None'. mypy/pyright will flag: 'Incompatible return value type (got InvoiceHeaderModel | None, expected InvoiceHeaderModel)'. Runtime-safe — the row was just flushed so the SELECT always finds it — but it is a static type error introduced by the I-001 fix.
issues.fix_instruction: After the second flush, guard the return: result = self.get(header.id); assert result is not None; return result. Alternatively use typing.cast: from typing import cast; return cast(InvoiceHeaderModel, self.get(header.id)).
issues.spec_ref: lld.json files[16] InvoiceRepository.create_with_lines output type: InvoiceHeaderModel (not Optional). plan.json DoD: create_with_lines is atomic.

summary: Major I-001 (lazy-load inconsistency) is resolved — create_with_lines now delegates to self.get(header.id) which uses the correct joinedload(lines, payments) path, matching the LLD spec and TC-189 expectation. SalesHeaderModel.header_id join column confirmed correct against transactions.py model. TC-187 (effective_from ordering), TC-188 (inactive price → None), and TC-189 (eager-loaded lines on create) are all satisfied. Three minor issues remain: I-002 (LSP parameter name mismatch in get()), I-003 (untyped data param in PaymentRepository.create), I-004 (return type annotation mismatch introduced by I-001 fix — InvoiceHeaderModel | None vs InvoiceHeaderModel). No critical or major issues. All DoD criteria met. Verdict: CLEAN.
